newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia prime ministers yet to reply - Sihanouk.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia prime ministers yet to reply - Sihanouk.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk has yet to receive a response from Cambodia's warring prime ministers to his appeal to meet in Beijing to hammer out a solution, he said a statement received on Monday.

Sihanouk issued his summons on Sunday to Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and his rival, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, as heavy fighting between their forces raged in the capital, Phnom Penh, for a second day.

"For the present, I have yet to receive their respective responses to my proposal," he said in a statement issued late on Sunday from his residence in Beijing, where he has been receiving medical treatment.
The king had called on both prime ministers as well as President of Parliament Chea Sim to come to Beijing and appealed for an unconditional end to the fighting.
Phnom Penh was quiet but tense as dawn broke on Monday but many residents feared a new round of fighting as forces loyal to the rival prime ministers faced off to the west of the city.
An explosion boomed across the capital from the west just as a 6 a.m. (2300 GMT) curfew ended after a night punctuated by intermittent bursts of small-arms fire.
At least 12 people were killed and more than 50 wounded in a weekend of fighting on the streets of the capital.
Hun Sen said in a radio broadcast late on Sunday that Ranariddh, who is Sihanouk's son, was a traitor and no longer held the post of first prime minister.
He called on the prince's party to choose a new person to fill the job. Ranariddh said in a statement from Paris at the weekend that Hun Sen had launched a coup against him.
The two leaders have shared power in a coalition government set up after a 1993 election organised by the United Nations.
As monarch, Sihanouk has little political power but is considered to retain wide popularity among the population of the battered Southeast Asian nation.
He has spent extended periods in Beijing since being deposed from power by a U.S.-backed 1970 coup and in recent years has frequently returned to the Chinese capital for medical treatment.
